title: Starmer trims budgets to fund extra £15bn for defence
summary_cn: 英国首相基尔·斯塔默宣布将国防开支增加150亿英镑，通过削减其他部门的投资预算来筹集资金，目标是在2029年前将年度国防预算提升至800亿英镑。此举旨在扭转军队的‘腐蚀性空心化’，但部分项目如道路和能源计划将被取消或调整。继任者预计为安迪·伯纳姆，他需在秋季预算中解决剩余的47亿英镑资金缺口。
paragraphs_en: Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has said a Â£15bn increase in military spending will be funded by cutting investment budgets in other areas, as he set out the UK's long-delayed plan to invest in defence.
In one of his final acts as prime minister, Sir Keir said some road and energy projects would not "go ahead as planned" to help raise defence funding to Â£80bn a year by 2029.
He said the plan would be built on by his successor, widely expected to be Andy Burnham, who is yet to comment on the plan.
The Treasury later confirmed only Â£10.3bn in savings had currently been identified, meaning Burnham would have to find the remaining Â£4.7bn in his first Budget in the autumn.

The extra Â£15bn in spending over the next four years is more than the Â£13.5bn secured by former Defence Secretary John Healey, who resigned earlier this month in protest at the plans, but less than the Â£28bn sought by defence chiefs.
In a speech, Sir Keir said the defence investment plan (DIP), initially expected last autumn, would reverse the "corrosive hollowing out" of the armed forces under the Conservatives.
Sir Keir said he had ruled out further borrowing to fund the increase, and instead the money would be found by cutting the long-term investment budgets of other government departments by 1%.
The Department for Transport (DfT) is making a further Â£700m in savings from roads projects, with the A38 Derby Junctions and A46 Newark Bypass scheme being considered for cancellation.
The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) is finding an additional Â£2bn from its budget. More detailed plans are expected in the autumn.
Some details of planned commitments over the next four years include:
More than Â£64bn to strengthen the UK's nuclear deterrent, including new submarines and F-35A fighter jets capable of carrying nuclear bombs
Â£5bn to fund a "drone transformation" for the armed forces
More than Â£8bn for the global combat air programme (Gcap), a scheme to build â¯the next generation of RAF stealth jets, in partnership with Japan and Italy
Plans for the Royal Navy to become a "hybrid navy", using self-controlled vessels and AI alongside warships and aircraft and funding for six new warships
The Royal Air Force will develop autonomous fighter jets and bring its "uncrewed electronic warfare drone system" into service in 2026

How much more is being spent on defence and will the UK hit Nato's targets?
Frank Gardner: Key points from government's defence spending plan
The DIP also says the Ministry of Defence (MoD) will attempt to make efficiency savings worth almost Â£11bn by 2030.
The MoD is planning to deliver the savings by reducing the civil service workforce, cutting back consultancy spending, and expanding the use of technology.
Defence officials say the increase in defence spending is not conditional on the savings being made.

The DIP also says a number of defence programmes have been scrapped, including Storm Shadow missiles, a new satellite system, and Wildcat utility helicopters, which will now be phased out in favour of an "autonomous replacement".
Sir Keir has pushed ahead with the DIP despite his impending departure from Downing Street after announcing his resignation last week.
Tense Whitehall negotiations over how to fund it have been ongoing for months.

Defence Secretary Dan Jarvis told BBC Newsnight he had discussed the investment plan with Burnham, but it is understood he could not be briefed on certain security issues and did not sign off the full thing.
Jarvis would not confirm if Burnham had been told that he would need to find an additional Â£4.7bn to fund the defence investment plan if he becomes prime minister.
Two defence ministers quit , with Armed Forces Minister Al Carns joining Healey in resigning over the scale of the proposed uplift.
In his speech, Sir Keir nodded to these difficulties, arguing "the hard truth is that there are no easy answers".

Sir Keir said the plan would now increase the military budget to 2.7% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2029, and put the UK on track to meet Nato's core defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035.
The prime minister said the UK was on track to spend 3% of GDP on defence in the next five-year Parliament - but he did not set a more specific date on this target, something Healey had called for.
The DIP says the plan to hit the 3% target would be set out at the next spending review, which is currently scheduled to take place next year.
The DIP follows the wide-ranging Strategic Defence Review (SDR), which was published in June 2025 and pledged billions in extra spending to fund a shift towards "warfighting readiness".
General Sir Richard Barrons, one of authors of SDR, said while the publication of the DIP "does count as progress", it would not "crack the issue" defending the UK "sufficiently well and quickly".
Speaking earlier, he said: "More has to be done sooner and that requires more money than is currently on the table".
Shadow defence secretary James Cartlidge said the prime minister had left a "legacy of failure", an "underfunded defence investment plan that's too little, too late".

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said the government had "dangerously short-changed our armed forces", meaning defence chiefs "have been forced to make hard choices, when they should be given what they need".

Nato General Secretary Mark Rutte has previously urged the alliance's members to present "clear, concrete and credible plans" for how they will raise defence spending to 3.5% ahead of a leaders' summit in Turkey next week.
Rutte welcomed the DIP as a "good step" towards the 3.5% target, saying "stronger UK defence makes us all safer".

paragraphs_cn: 首相基尔·斯塔默爵士（Sir Keir Starmer）表示，将通过削减其他领域的投资预算来为150亿英镑的军费增长提供资金，他同时公布了英国长期拖延的国防投资计划。
作为首相的最后举措之一，基尔爵士表示，一些道路和能源项目将不会“按原计划推进”，以帮助在2029年前将国防经费提高到每年800亿英镑。
他表示，该计划将由他的继任者（普遍预计是安迪·伯纳姆，Andy Burnham）继续推进，伯纳姆尚未对此计划发表评论。
财政部随后确认，目前仅确定了103亿英镑的节余，这意味着伯纳姆必须在秋季的首份预算中自行找到剩余的47亿英镑。
未来四年额外增加的150亿英镑支出，超过了前国防大臣约翰·希利（John Healey）本月早些时候因抗议该计划而辞职时所争取的135亿英镑，但低于国防首长们寻求的280亿英镑。
基尔爵士在一次演讲中表示，原定于去年秋季公布的国防投资计划（DIP）将扭转保守党执政期间对军队“腐蚀性的掏空”。
基尔爵士称，他已排除通过进一步借贷来为增资提供资金的可能性，而是通过将其他政府部门的长期投资预算削减1%来筹集资金。
交通部（DfT）正从道路项目中进一步节省7亿英镑，其中A38德比枢纽和A46纽瓦克绕道项目正在考虑取消。
能源安全与净零排放部（DESNZ）正从其预算中额外节省20亿英镑。更详细的计划预计将于秋季公布。
未来四年计划承诺的一些细节包括：
超过640亿英镑用于加强英国的核威慑力量，包括新型潜艇和能够携带核弹的F-35A战斗机
50亿英镑用于军队的“无人机转型”
超过80亿英镑用于全球空战计划（Gcap），该计划旨在与日本和意大利合作建造下一代英国皇家空军隐形战斗机
皇家海军计划成为“混合海军”，使用自主舰艇和人工智能，同时配备军舰和飞机，并资助建造六艘新军舰
皇家空军将开发自主战斗机，并于2026年将“无人电子战无人机系统”投入使用

观看：安全事务记者弗兰克·加德纳分析政府长期拖延的国防计划
国防开支实际增加了多少，英国能否达到北约的目标？
弗兰克·加德纳：政府国防开支计划的要点
国防投资计划还指出，国防部（MoD）将力争到2030年实现近110亿英镑的效率节余。
国防部计划通过减少公务员队伍、削减咨询支出以及扩大技术使用来实现这些节余。
国防官员表示，国防开支的增加并不以这些节余的实现为条件。
国防投资计划还表示，一些国防项目已被取消，包括风暴阴影导弹、一个新卫星系统以及野猫通用直升机，这些将被逐步淘汰，转而采用“自主替代方案”。
尽管基尔爵士上周宣布辞职后即将离开唐宁街，但他仍坚持推进国防投资计划。
白厅关于如何为其提供资金的紧张谈判已持续数月。
国防大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）告诉BBC《新闻之夜》，他已与伯纳姆讨论了该投资计划，但据了解，他无法就某些安全问题向伯纳姆通报，也没有签署全部内容。
贾维斯不愿证实伯纳姆是否被告知，如果他成为首相，将需要额外找到47亿英镑来资助国防投资计划。
两位国防部长辞职，武装部队部长阿尔·卡恩斯（Al Carns）与希利一同因拟议的增资规模而辞职。
基尔爵士在演讲中提到了这些困难，称“残酷的事实是没有简单的答案”。
基尔爵士表示，该计划将在2029年前将军事预算提高到国内生产总值（GDP）的2.7%，并使英国有望在2035年前达到北约核心国防开支目标，即GDP的3.5%。
首相表示，英国有望在下一个五年议会任期内将国防开支提高到GDP的3%——但他没有为此目标设定更具体的日期，而这是希利所呼吁的。
国防投资计划称，实现3%目标的计划将在下一次支出审查中公布，该审查目前定于明年进行。
国防投资计划是在2025年6月发布的广泛战略防务评估（SDR）之后制定的，该评估承诺额外支出数十亿英镑，以推动向“战备状态”的转变。
战略防务评估的作者之一理查德·巴伦斯爵士（General Sir Richard Barrons）表示，虽然国防投资计划的发布“确实算是一种进展”，但它不会“足够好、足够快地解决”保卫英国的问题。
他早些时候表示：“必须更快地做更多事情，这需要比目前摆在桌面上的更多的资金。”
影子国防大臣詹姆斯·卡特利奇（James Cartlidge）表示，首相留下了“失败的遗产”，一个“资金不足的国防投资计划，太少、太迟”。
自由民主党领袖埃德·戴维爵士（Sir Ed Davey）表示，政府“危险地亏待了我们的武装部队”，这意味着国防首长们“被迫做出艰难选择，而他们本应得到所需的一切”。
北约秘书长马克·吕特（Mark Rutte）此前敦促联盟成员在下周于土耳其举行的领导人峰会之前，就如何将国防开支提高到3.5%提出“明确、具体和可信的计划”。
吕特对国防投资计划表示欢迎，称这是朝着3.5%目标迈出的“良好一步”，并表示“更强大的英国国防让我们所有人都更安全”。
